title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Seriously Studying and Implementing the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Litigation Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases
keywords_en: application for retrial; foreign-related civil and commercial cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Earnestly Studying and Implementing the Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-related Civil and Commercial Cases

Fa [2002] No. 22

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

For the purpose of meeting the needs arising from China's accession to the World Trade Organization, handling foreign-related civil and commercial cases in accordance with the law in a timely and impartial manner, and effectively protecting the lawful rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties, the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court recently adopted the Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-related Civil and Commercial Cases (hereinafter referred to as the Provisions, the full text of which is set out on page 52 of this issue). For the purpose of studying and implementing this judicial interpretation, the following notice is hereby given:

1. It is necessary to deeply understand the important significance of implementing the Provisions and to complete all preparatory work as soon as possible. The centralized jurisdiction over foreign-related civil and commercial cases is an important reform measure adopted in response to the new situation after the accession to the WTO; it is an important decision made to optimize case jurisdiction and fully utilize the effectiveness of adjudication. All higher people's courts shall actively carry out preparatory work, promptly clarify the regional divisions of courts exercising centralized jurisdiction in accordance with the requirements of the Provisions, and ensure timely operation, firmly safeguarding the overall national interest and the uniformity of the legal system.

2. Intermediate people's courts that have jurisdiction over foreign-related civil and commercial cases under the Provisions shall establish trial divisions dedicated to hearing foreign-related civil and commercial cases. In regions where such cases are relatively few, intermediate people's courts shall establish specialized collegial panels.

3. In light of the characteristics of foreign-related civil and commercial adjudication work, effective measures shall be taken to vigorously carry out various forms of professional training, so that judges handling foreign-related civil and commercial cases can quickly become familiar with the rules of the World Trade Organization, relevant international conventions, and international practices, and strive to build a team of expert-type foreign-related civil and commercial adjudicators who are well-versed in law, international trade, and foreign languages.

4. Applications for retrial and petition cases concerning effective judgments in foreign-related civil and commercial cases shall be handled by the trial division of the people's court responsible for hearing foreign-related civil and commercial cases. For applications for retrial and petition cases concerning effective judgments in foreign-related civil and commercial cases rendered by the court at the same level, the trial supervision division shall be responsible for handling them.

5. All higher people's courts shall strengthen supervision over and coordination of the implementation of centralized jurisdiction, and actively carry out relevant work. Problems encountered during the implementation of the Provisions shall be promptly reported to this Court.

This notice is hereby given.

March 1, 2002
